LESSON: MOVEMENT OF MATERIALS IN AND OUT OF THE CELL

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 2.2: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Movement of Materials in and out of the cell, part of Living Things and their Environment in Grade 8 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How do materials move in and out of a cell?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use print and non-print material to search for information on the processes involved in the movement of materials in and out of a cell, discuss with peers (cover diffusion and osmosis),

2. carry out experiments to demonstrate diffusion in plant materials and share the findings with peers,

3. carry out experiments to demonstrate osmosis using visking tubing and plant materials, and share their findings with peers,

4. search for information from print and non-print media on the roles of diffusion and osmosis in living things and discuss with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print and non-print material to search for information on the processes involved in the movement of materials in and out of a cell, discuss with peers (cover diffusion and osmosis),
2. carry out experiments to demonstrate diffusion in plant materials and share the findings with peers,
3. carry out experiments to demonstrate osmosis using visking tubing and plant materials, and share their findings with peers,
4. search for information from print and non-print media on the roles of diffusion and osmosis in living things and discuss with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Movement of Materials in and out of the cell together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: the learner acquires writing skills while recording findings from experiments to

demonstrate diffusion and osmosis.

• Self-efficacy: the learner executes assigned tasks successfully while carrying out experiments to demonstrate diffusion and

osmosis.

Values:
• Respect: the learner appreciates the opinions of peers when discussing the roles of diffusion and osmosis in living

things.

• Responsibility: the learner executes assigned roles while carrying out experiments to demonstrate diffusion and

osmosis.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental conservation: the learner learns how to disposes of waste materials from experiments to demonstrate

diffusion and osmosis appropriately.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to link the information on diffusion and osmosis to absorption of water and mineral salts from the soil by

crops in Agriculture.
